summary: An arrow's label now sits on one of ten chip styles picked from picture tiles, with a marker (none, accent, error, warning, done, info) at its front. The chip follows the arrow's colour and its words always read.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/chip-styles-walk.json. Sheets drawn by the real renderer: PHOTONZ_CHIP_SHEET=<dir> Scripts/test.sh --filter ChipStyleRendering.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press A and drag an arrow, type a label and press Command Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In Appearance, click each of the ten Chip tiles under the arrow Style tiles and watch the label change.
Pick a different colour for the line: the chip's plate follows it, light colours taking dark words.
Click Error, Warning, Done or Info in the Marker row; Accent brings the style's own stripe or dot back.
Draw a second arrow: it starts in the chip you picked last.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right click the arrow: Chip Style sits beside Arrow Style.
Export the picture as a PNG and compare the chip with the canvas.

evaluate: Is Solid pill the right look for a new label, or should Paper or Hairline be the default?
Do Glass, Spec badge, Lit tag and Highlighter earn their tiles, or should the set drop to the ones that read as professional?
Does the Marker row read as a choice of icon at a glance?
Is it clear that the chip follows the line colour without opening anything?
rough: An independent model judge scored the sheet against Apple's apps, Figma and Sketch redline plugins and CleanShot X: Solid pill 7, Flat squircle 7, Hairline 8, Paper 8, Two-tone 7 pass; Glass 4, Spec badge 6, Lit tag 6, Highlighter 4 and Today 5 do not (the baseline red pill scored 5). The task stays open on that bar.

Glass is drawn at 95 to 97 percent opacity, not the design system's 82, because the app blends in linear light and 82 percent fell to 3.2:1 over white; it reads as a tinted plate with a lit rim rather than frosted glass. A true blur of the picture under it is not built (written into docs/design/markup.md section 3).
Measurements do not wear chip styles yet: filed as every-measurement-wears-the-same-chip-styles-col.
The five new arrow styles (Dashed, Block, Neon, Dotted, Elbow) are not built: filed as five-more-arrow-styles-dashed-block-neon-dotted.

Appearance is not yet the simplified Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size with a collapsed Advanced (markup.md section 8), and there is no Size S M L yet: filed as arrow-and-measurement-appearance-shows-only-styl. The Label size and Label corners sliders are still there.

A walk's press on a dock tile button does nothing (Arrow Style tiles too, since 2026-10-26), so no walk can yet prove the tiles by pointer: chip-styles-picking-walk is written and owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26.
An SVG export draws the chip's plate, edge and words in the style's colours but not its finish (gradient, rim, shadow, marker, monospace).
While typing, the bubble shows the style's plate and shadow but not its accent or marker; they land on commit.
